turns.text: it's 3:40 and i'm dead. just came off shift and sat through the paid 8 hour charting training this morning. i normally sleep 8:30 to 3 with blackout curtains and a box fan and that obviously didn't happen. how much sleep do i need before tonight and when should i cut off caffeine

Rough day. Here's the short version:

- Sleep: aim for a nap of 90 minutes (one full cycle) or 3-4 hours if you can get it. Even 90 minutes helps a lot.
- Timing: sleep as soon as you can, and set an alarm so you wake at least 2-3 hours before you need to be alert. Waking up from deep sleep right before work makes grogginess worse.
- Caffeine: it stays active for roughly 5-6 hours (half-life), so keep it out of the pre-nap window. Skip it for at least 6 hours before you try to sleep. Use it after you wake, and again early in your shift, then taper off in the second half so you can sleep afterward.
- Also: dim lights, cool room, bright light when you wake.

What time do you need to be up and when does your shift start?
shift starts 7. i'm heading to ruiz family market for fish sauce and produce on the way home, want something to eat before bed. also is a second thermos of cà phê sữa đá too much for tonight

Plan for the nap:

- Eat light: something with protein and some carbs, not heavy or greasy. Eggs and rice, or a rice bowl with veg and a little protein, or yogurt and fruit. A big meal can disrupt sleep.
- Nap: get home, eat, then sleep about 3-4 hours, and set an alarm for about 3 hours before your shift so you have time to wake up.
- Caffeine: no coffee until after you wake.

On the second thermos: for a long night, two thermoses of cà phê sữa đá is usually in the range of 400 mg or a bit more, depending on how strong you brew. That's about the upper limit for most adults per day. Since you're running on a sleep deficit, I'd do this: drink the first thermos in the first half of your shift, and only open the second if you really need it around midnight to 2 a.m. Stop by about 3 a.m. so you can fall asleep after. If you're jittery or your heart races, skip the second.
